function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find nearby public libraries in Boston, MA that have an English fiction section and free Wi-Fi. We need to use the provided function public_library_find_nearby. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]}) => any.

We need to pass location: "Boston, MA". Facilities: we need Wi-Fi and Fiction. The facilities parameter expects a single value? It says type: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That seems ambiguous: maybe it's a union of strings or array of strings? The description says "Facilities and sections in public library." So maybe we can pass an array of strings? But the type says "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe" type? That seems weird. Possibly they want an array of strings: ["Wi-Fi", "Fiction"]. But the type says "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[] which is a union of string literal types and an array type. That is confusing. But likely we should pass an array of strings: ["Wi-Fi", "Fiction"].

Thus call the function with location: "Boston, MA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Fiction"].

We then output the result.
